A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AdaSplash research. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-C are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered tables.

before.justification: V1 reports original efficiency measurements and trained-model results for retrieval, classification, language understanding, and language modeling, with additional results in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains these original efficiency measurements and downstream experimental results in the main text and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The Halley-bisection procedure, tiled attention computation, optional block masking, pointer lookup tables, and backward-pass kernels remain unchanged. Algorithms 1-5 and Appendix A retain the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic efficiency scenarios, FineWeb/FineWeb-Edu training data, MS MARCO and BEIR retrieval tasks, GLUE, ECtHR classification, and HellaSwag evaluation. No dataset, task, or evaluated domain is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the matched experiments, including CUDA/Triton FlashAttention-2 and Torch sorting/bisection. Top-k attention and Native Sparse Attention appear only in the expanded related-work discussion, not as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the experimental settings, including the three-versus-ten iteration efficiency comparison, synthetic sequence lengths of 1k-64k, 2B-token encoder pretraining, and 10B-token GPT-2 training. Metrics, model configurations, precision, and gradient-accumulation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The convergence comparison, masked-versus-unmasked efficiency comparison, context-length analyses, attention-head sparsity heatmaps, and validation-loss curves are retained. The relocated long-document efficiency table supplies no new ablation or supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging activation runtimes over 1,000 runs and GPT-2 runtimes over 50 steps after at least 100 training steps. Neither introduces new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: All matched table values and the results plotted in Figures 1-6 are unchanged. V1 Table 6 reappears as v2 Table 3, while v1 Tables 3-5 become v2 Tables 4-6. For example, dense and sparse GPT-2 validation losses remain 3.283 and 3.263.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Halley/bisection updates, Jacobian, gradient derivations, and memory-complexity arguments are unchanged. Equations 1-30 and the derivations in Appendix A contain no substantive revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: faster entmax computation, sparsity-aware Triton kernels, competitive efficiency relative to FlashAttention-2, and strong downstream performance. The stated sevenfold reduction in iteration count is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds an explicit interpretation of the existing long-document efficiency measurements, describing Torch bisection as infeasible for most realistic training setups and AdaSplash as enabling practical training at costs close to dense attention. V1 presented these measurements without this task-specific feasibility discussion; existing mechanism explanations and limitations remain.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, training recipes, hardware, and code/data access information are retained. Moving the code link to the first page and shortening the H100 description do not change reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds citations to Top-k attention (Gupta et al., 2021) and Native Sparse Attention (Yuan et al., 2025), contrasting their stated fixed sparsity budgets with entmax's input-dependent transformation. It also expands discussion of already-cited BigBird and refines positioning relative to Reformer and Routing Transformer.

P1.justification: V2 adds the long-document efficiency discussion and locally rewrites the sparse-attention related-work paragraph. It also updates affiliations, correspondence information, acknowledgments, and some wording, while retaining the section organization and most prose.

P2.justification: The full-width appendix Table 6 becomes main-text Table 3, reformatted into stacked runtime and memory panels with a revised caption. Other tables are renumbered, the GPT-2 table and Figure 4 shift position, and publication information alters first-page layout. No new figure or table content is introduced.

improvement.justification: Moving the existing long-document efficiency table into Section 4.2 and explaining its implications makes the practical efficiency evidence easier to assess. The focused Top-k and Native Sparse Attention discussion also clarifies research positioning. These are modest gains in clarity and context; the method, experimental evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
